answer: Dual-path timing audit. Each identity answers a nonce seeded by a public beacon over two routes each round. The first crosses a karst of uneven relay hops, yielding an unpredictable delay profile. The second runs along a stable ridge, yielding a near-constant one. Verifiers check the arrival-time pair against that identity's history. Clones can copy keys but not independent timing histories; a shared host emits correlated vectors and gets flagged. Each extra identity thus needs its own network vantage, clock discipline, and continuous participation, costing more than its fixed reward cap.
